title: refactor(core): dashboard date presets read their bounds from the spec window table
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbV2JyEd3XiA89ZqaTUz4Nwt)_

Fixes #29116

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:仪表盘日期筛选不再自带一份预设日期区间表,13 个预设(本月、上季度、近 30 天等)一律读 spec 里那张唯一的表。
- 为什么改:两张表写的是同一组区间,只是本期写法不同(`{current_month_start}` 对 `{month_start}`),迟早会漂移;你已定为低优先级卡。
- 风险与回滚:本期区间的写法从 `{current_*}` 换成同义的 `{month_start}` 这类别名,解析出的日期逐一相同;回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts` 里的 `presetBounds`,然后是新测试 `dashboard-filters.presetWindows-29116.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:在 `ui/` 下运行 `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/dashboard-filters.presetWindows-29116.test.ts`,应看到 44 个测试全部通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- `ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts`: the local `PRESET_RANGES` table is gone. `presetBounds(preset)` now returns the spec's window from `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), and membership is decided by the spec's exact `isDateRangePresetName`, both in `presetBounds` and in `normalizeDateDefault` (which used `defaultValue in PRESET_RANGES`). The docblocks that explained the table's `satisfies` pin now say where that guarantee lives: the spec declaration is typed `Record<DateRangePreset, …>`, so a preset added without a window fails to compile in the spec, and there is no local table to invent a name in.
- The emitted condition for the four current-period presets changes spelling only: `this_week`, `this_month`, `this_quarter` and `this_year` emit the bare aliases (`{month_start}` / `{month_end}` and so on) instead of `{current_month_start}` / `{current_month_end}`. The other nine presets emit byte-identical tokens.
- No new key, option, schema or export. No spec change. `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` is still re-exported from `@object-ui/core` as before.
- Patch changeset `.changeset/29116-dashboard-preset-windows-from-spec.md` for `@object-ui/core`.

## Why

The card: the same 13 presets had two tables, the spec's and this module's, in two spellings of the same days. Both resolve today through `DATE_MACRO_ALIAS_TOKENS`, so nothing was wrong on screen; the risk was the tables drifting.

## Tests

New `ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/dashboard-filters.presetWindows-29116.test.ts` (44 tests):

- every preset in `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` emits exactly the spec's window (13 cases), and the preset set equals the retired table's 13 keys;
- every preset resolves (`resolveDateMacros`) to the same two calendar dates under the new spelling and under the retired `{current_*}` table, copied verbatim into the test, on six reference dates that cross week, month, quarter and year boundaries plus a leap day (13 cases);
- for a compare-to widget fed the same condition, `shiftFilterByCompareTo` gives the same window for `previousPeriod` and `previousYear`, and `compareToTrendLabelKey` gives the same label under both spellings (13 cases);
- a stored dashboard written in the `{current_*}` spelling still filters: a custom range `{ from: '{current_month_start}', to: '{current_month_end}' }` passes through and selects the same days as the `this_month` preset, and a date global filter defaulting to `'{current_quarter_start}'` is kept as a token, passed through and resolved;
- an unknown preset still misses with the usual warning, including names that are `Object.prototype` members (`constructor`, `toString`, `__proto__`), and such a name is not lifted to `{ preset }` as a date default.

Changed pin: `ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/dashboard-filters.test.ts` asserted the literal `{current_month_start}` / `{current_month_end}` emitted for `this_month` (two places). They now assert `{month_start}` / `{month_end}`. This is behaviour-neutral: the pin is on the emitted token string, and the parity cases above prove the two tokens resolve to the same day on every preset and reference date.

Pins named by the card stay green without edits: `ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/report-chart-query-spec-parity.test.ts`, the plugin-dashboard `DashboardFilterBar*` and `DashboardRenderer.filters` tests (none of them pins an emitted current-period token).

## Acceptance notes

- One small behaviour difference on junk input: a stored preset name that only matched an inherited object member (for example `'constructor'`) used to pass the old `in` check, then resolved to no bounds and was dropped with no warning. It is now dropped with the standard unknown-preset warning. Covered by the prototype-member cases above.
- The spec docblock on `DATE_RANGE_PRESET_MACRO_WINDOWS` says the console's lowering "stays the executable mapping" and the table is "deliberately NOT a resolver". That still reads true (the lowering stays in `dashboard-filters`, it now reads the table), so the spec is left untouched as the card requires.
- Open PRs whose search hits name `dashboard-filters` (#29162, #29263, #29295, #29251) do not touch `dashboard-filters.ts`.
